evidence:
Inspected the actual frozen root and bundled XLSX with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 48/check 47 says "Shared pinned judge agent + model, pinned judge CLIs and browser" and explicitly says temperature/prompt-version markers are unnecessary and public networking/missing allowlists are not defects. Internal Quality Checks row 48 has older temperature-0/versioned-prompt wording; the shipped profile and frozen skill Delivery profile/quality-checks.md:187-189 control interpretation.

All 50 frozen task files and all 34 frozen rules files matched manifest SHA256 entries. task/task.toml:30-35 specifies REWARDKIT_JUDGE="claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx" and the exact shared provider/environment block; parsed equality with the frozen template succeeded. Parsed all five gates/scored judge.toml files: every [judge] selects only the expected claude-code fallback, has no model/reasoning_effort/temperature override, and every Playwright MCP uses --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium. task/tests/Dockerfile:16-21 pins claude-code@2.1.281, codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 and app dependencies; :31 pins harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7; :33-38 installs Chromium via that installed MCP package's bundled Playwright CLI and links the shared executable. The complete verifier Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template. The shared score.py, restart_mcp.py, test.sh and scoring.toml also match the template byte for byte (score SHA256 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e; restart SHA256 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5). No task-specific tool-build drift found.

There is no date-dependent business rule or calendar-valued seed to freeze. environment/instructions/behaviour.md:9 asks for five seconds of elapsed execution including callbacks; :19-21 asks for elapsed run durations and an approximately two-second typing pause. The empty seed contains no dates. All five prompts and all criteria were scanned for clock/date/timing dependencies. Functional prompt:15 measures from the real Run/interaction action with about eight seconds scheduling allowance; :113 requires timed fixtures and bounded waits in one browser call, explicitly rejecting time between model replies. S16:370 accepts seconds/milliseconds and rounding, compares short versus delayed runs and allows a broad 3-8 second duration. S17:377-381 measures the app's actual debounce before scheduling follow-up edits, rather than imposing one millisecond constant. S36:446-455 observes callback markers through ten seconds in a single browser call instead of distinguishing model/tool reply times. Date.now at prompt:36 produces a unique locally intercepted network-control nonce; it never defines a scored calendar value. test.sh:178's UTC date is a restart log annotation only.

Adversarial source checks: a conforming alternative with a 1.2-second debounce and durations displayed as rounded seconds remains admissible under S17 and S16; changing the execution date leaves all their expected values unchanged. A broken implementation that resets the five-second budget on each callback would permit the inner 3+3-second completion marker at six seconds; S36 explicitly rejects that marker after a working short nested-timer control. These are source-level counterfactual checks, not new app/provider runs.

Raw RESULTS.json SHA256 was independently verified as ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09, matching raw-evidence-index.json. Its recorded Chromium is Google Chrome for Testing 152.0.7977.8 and MCP is Version 0.0.79; launch_workflow.py:34 records these through actual --version subprocesses. The launch/current/runtime/core driver hashes inspected matched the raw report. The raw S36 evidence contains nested-control-done, late-callback-entered, a five-second time-limit error, no forbidden-nested-completion, and successful recovery. workflow_core.cjs:10 uses monotonic process.hrtime for scripted observation timing. This supports the local browser setup only. Full configured LLM judge repeatability, duration, Oracle and target-model behavior remain unmeasured, as the raw index explicitly states; this source-pinning Pass makes none of those claims.
